claims.text: Mechanical-property differences among equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni and its subsets are governed by the interaction of lattice distortion, stacking-fault energy, and grain-boundary characteristics.
Lattice distortion, stacking-fault energy, and grain-boundary characteristics influence dislocation glide and twinning-mediated plasticity.
The investigated materials are equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni and its quaternary and ternary subsets in a single-phase FCC state after thermomechanical processing.
Changing the constituent elements alters lattice distortion.
Changing the constituent elements alters stacking-fault energy.
Changing the constituent elements alters grain-boundary characteristics.
Dislocation glide and twinning-mediated plasticity are the mechanisms connecting the proposed structural mediators to mechanical behavior.
Relative to alloys with lower lattice distortion, alloys with higher lattice distortion will have higher strength.
Relative to alloys with higher stacking-fault energy, alloys with lower stacking-fault energy will have higher strength.
Alloys with higher lattice distortion and lower stacking-fault energy will have lower ductility.
Alloys with lower lattice distortion and higher stacking-fault energy will have lower strength and higher ductility.
The proposed relationship is limited to single-phase FCC alloys composed only of Cr, Mn, Fe, Co, and Ni.
The exact relationships among lattice distortion, stacking-fault energy, grain-boundary characteristics, and mechanical properties are not well established.
